US: Saipan lodgment survives D-Day with about 20-22.5k combat troops ashore but a shallow/disorganized beachhead and 3.3-4.1k combat casualties. TF58 retains 16 fast decks; submarine warning keeps about 12 decks local while one 4-deck group handles short Bonins suppression.
Japan_ground: Saipan opens with 57-64 ready armored vehicles, including 18-22 Shinhoto Type 97. Daytime packet tactics preserve much of the regiment; end-day 48-56 armored vehicles remain ready and the 16/17 Jun mass-counterattack gate is still open.
Japan_land_air: End-day onsite ready 58-78, fighters 27-39, attack/recon 18-27. Local air cannot restore air superiority but can still scout and strike small targets.
Japan_mobile: Five-carrier core remains 356-379 ready; six secondary carriers 143-179 combat-usable; seven available battleships in the battle system. Main force is roughly 700-850 nmi WSW of Saipan by late day.
ISR: US submarine fusion confirms a major Japanese carrier-battleship sortie but lacks continuous weapon-quality shadowing. Japanese predelegated Sixth Fleet control avoids a full Saipan-HQ command collapse; a probable US fast-carrier sector is obtained but remains too broad/stale for a 15 Jun fleet strike.
next_focus: 16 Jun: Bonins suppression/return, Japanese fleet refueling/search geometry, US submarine recontact, Japanese submarine patrol-line contacts, Saipan beachhead consolidation, and whether local/mobilized Japanese air can produce a useful carrier or fire-support target fix.
